label: Foundational Questions of Belief
reader_question: Okay, but how would I even know God is real — and isn't it a bit much to say faith is just built into me?
one_line: The foundational layer only: what kind of thing God is claimed to be (not a 'thing' at all), how a finite being could come to know the Absolute, and the four classical routes by which God's existence is held to be provable.

key_claims.quote: We must acknowledge first that our very nature points in the direction of the infinite by being able to perceive the effects of things greater than ourselves and that this being the only nature we possess, there is no other choice, but to accept these intuitive conceptions. When we perceive purpose and design in the whole of reality we are understanding the nature of the product and that something is behind it.

key_claims.quote: So, to begin, we are intuitively aware of that which is greater than us and it is an essential aspect of our humanity.

key_claims.quote:
Here, Allah states that the signs which point to Truth can be found “in the horizons” (external) “and within us” (internal). As such, the principle arguments for God’s existence may also be divided under these two categories. This dichotomy results in various methods by which such arguments may be validated. For instance, Shaykh Abu ‘Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Saalih ibn Muhammad ibn al-Uthaymeen at-Tamimi categorizes these methods into four in his Commentary on the Three Fundamental Principles of Islam:
His existence, Exalted is He, may be proven by the Fiṭrah (one’s natural inclination), the intellect [Aql], the legislation [Shari’ah], and the senses [Hawass].[4]
key_claims.supports: what are the four ways god existence is proven in islam

key_claims.quote: The word fitrah is derived from the Arabic root fatara, which means ‘to create’, thus the former might be translated as “a way of being created”.[9]

key_claims.quote: Upon establishing the appropriate understanding of the fitrah and its existence as a normative aspect of humanity, we can move on to elucidating how it functions. This is perhaps the most important part of this article in that it sets the stage for establishing the foundational arguments for God’s existence from the Islamic perspective.

key_claims.quote: The philosophical support behind the intuition is based on the recognition that: (1) there are such things as ‘reality’ and ‘knowledge’, and (2) that human beings can grasp both at a normative level of cognition.

key_claims.quote: The concept of God is not some innate belief, but is inferred from the mind’s own inner workings, which are not bound by the constraints of natural laws – that is why we are able to ‘see’ beyond direct observations and conceive of abstract notions (theories) which make them coherent.

key_claims.quote: For believers in the Divine, God’s existence is in fact quite an ordinary aspect of reality; something easily grasped by the mind and deduced from basic internal and external observations.

notes: HONEST SCOPE VERDICT: this is the smallest cluster and it is thin for one of its two assigned halves. The 'whether God exists / how would one know' half is genuinely well covered. The 'basic articles of belief' half is NOT COVERED AT ALL. A grep of _posts/ and _transcripts/ for tawhid, aqeedah, shahada, pillars of faith, articles of belief and six fundamentals returns no substantive treatment: the only real hit is one passing use of tawhid inside a footnote-level argument in Part 1 line 81 (corruption of the fitrah is 'a suppression of a proper understanding of tawhid'), and the shahada hits are in an unrelated story post and a book-list post. There is no creed text, no pillars-of-iman exposition, no tawhid explainer anywhere in the recovered corpus. Do not let a page built on this file imply otherwise. RECOMMENDATION: build the page, but scope it as 'how we come to know God exists', not as a general aqeedah primer, and expect a thin page. EXCLUDE ON ATTRIBUTION GROUNDS - 'Adam Is No Myth' (2020-08-07, _posts/2020-08-07-adam-is-no-myth.md) is CONFIRMED a republication of Dr David Jalajel's own response and is deliberately NOT filed as material anywhere in this cluster. Verified independently: the post's own image alt text reads 'Dr David Jalajel, author of “Adam is No Myth”'; line 28 has Jalajel writing in the first person ('I wish to discuss some confusion... I have been encouraged to respond to these allegations by Asadullah Ali, Shoaib Malik, and others'), so Al-Andalusi appears as a third party who encouraged the response, not as the author; the whole body is Jalajel's first-person defence of his 2018 paper and of his book Islam & Biological Evolution (2009); and the top-of-post notes say 'This is a response by Dr. David Jalajel to criticisms of his paper'. The post front-matter still says author: Asadullah Ali Al-Andalusi because it is his site's republication - the archive must not attribute this argument to him. It is also off-topic here even on the merits: its subject is Adam, evolution and sam'iyyat, not the existence of God. WHAT THE SEED TITLES ACTUALLY ARGUE (read, not inferred). 'Nothing' (2012-01-13, 335 words) is a short note on the word 'nothing' and the word 'thing'. It argues that absolute non-existence is incoherent ('there is only existence'), that no object we can call a 'thing' conforms to the Absolute, and that 'nothing' must therefore be read as No-Thing, the transcendent reality that words cannot reach. It is a metaphysics-of-language note that ends 'All that is, was once Nothing.' It is NOT a piece about atheism, and it contains no argument from anything. 'How to know “No-thing”' (2012-01-19, 564 words) is the direct answer to the cluster's central question, and is the most important text in the file. It opens by naming the objection outright - 'Many may be wondering then how we come to know of this nothingness if in our finitude we are unable to grasp that which is beyond us' - and answers it from our nature pointing toward the infinite, refutes the projection objection, refutes the fallacy-of-composition reply, and closes 'This we call God.' It is a compressed, early, first-person statement of the same intuition/fitrah position he develops at length in 2015-2016. It also forward-references a note titled 'Why Kalaam Fails' which is NOT present anywhere in this repository (checked _posts/, _articles/, _data/canonical_works.json, _data/lost_works.json) - a real and currently undocumented gap, since it is cited as already having touched the epistemics of knowing the Nothing. OVERLAP WITH _data/topics/atheism-doubt.json - READ THIS BEFORE PUBLISHING. That sibling file has already claimed the two-part essay 'The Rationality of Believing in God Without Evidence' (6 quotes from Part 1, 10 from Part 2), 'Extraordinary Claims Require Extraordinary Evidence' (3 quotes), 'How to know No-thing' (3 quotes, framed as rebutting the projection charge and naturalism self-defeating), 'Nothing' (1 quote), and parts of transcript-NyAVl7RsEOs, lZkv38vd7bw, BRDaCqipcwM, lS7h9SKJtVc, ZbcsxAoIVY0, 1U6VfHosrqw, WED5mPmO_yU and X36xEj0OSV4. There is no recovered text anywhere in the repository that argues the traditional proofs of God's existence on their merits - no Kalam reconstruction, no contingency argument worked through, no design argument defended on its own terms. He explicitly declines the first two in the Part 5 Q&A: he says Kalam and its like 'help to solidify the belief of the believer' and 'don't help with atheists', and that 'other than the fitra, I don't like those arguments'. Anyone searching 'proof of god's existence' expecting a classical proof will not find one here; the archive should say so rather than imply the page delivers it.
